lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 5 you met ancient India. Which number did Indian mathematicians write as a digit, which Europe later took up? (Zero.) Today: the Mughal emperors who ruled much of India from 1526.

In 1526 Babur, a prince from Central Asia, won the battle of Panipat and founded the Mughal Empire. He was descended from Genghis Khan and Timur. Mughal comes from the Persian word for Mongol. The empire lasted until 1857.

His grandson Akbar became emperor in 1556, aged 13, and ruled for 49 years. He made friends and allies of Hindu Rajput princes. He ended a special tax on non-Muslims in 1564. Trained officials ran his empire, with a fairer land tax.

Akbar was curious about every faith. In 1575, at his new city of Fatehpur Sikri, he built a House of Worship. There Muslims, Hindus, Jains, Zoroastrians and Christians debated. It is said he could not read, but his great library was read aloud to him.

Mughal art mixed Persian and Indian styles: miniature paintings, carpets, and buildings of red sandstone and white marble. Shah Jahan (ruled 1628-1658) built the Taj Mahal at Agra. It is a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631.

About 20,000 workers built it from 1632, and with its gardens it was finished by about 1653. It is perfectly symmetrical: the tomb stands at the end of a four-part garden, a charbagh, split by water channels, with the river Yamuna behind.

Mughal India was one of the richest places on Earth. Its cotton cloth, such as calico and chintz, was traded worldwide, with indigo dye, spices and jewels. European trading companies came to buy them: you will meet them this year.

Try it in the world: build a symmetrical garden: four equal parts split by two water channels, a pool where they cross, and a white domed tomb at one end. Check that both halves match. Next: Ming China and Edo Japan.

exercises.prompt: Who founded the Mughal Empire in 1526?
exercises.hint: He won the battle of Panipat.
exercises.explain: Babur, a prince from Central Asia.

exercises.hint: He built it for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
exercises.explain: Shah Jahan built it at Agra as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, from 1632.

exercises.prompt: Akbar became emperor at the age of 13.
exercises.hint: He came to the throne very young.

exercises.explain: A tomb, for Mumtaz Mahal and later Shah Jahan too.

exercises.prompt: What did Mughal India sell to the world?
exercises.explain: Cotton cloth such as calico and chintz, spices, indigo dye and jewels.

exercises.prompt: Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605. For how many years?
exercises.hint: Take the first year from the last.

exercises.prompt: Work on the Taj Mahal began in 1632 and it was finished about 1653. About how many years did it take?
exercises.hint: Take the first year from the last.

exercises.prompt: Match each emperor to what he is known for.
exercises.hint: Founder, thinker, builder, and the last great emperor.
exercises.explain: Babur founded it; Akbar held the debates; Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal; under Aurangzeb it was largest.

exercises.prompt: In a charbagh garden, what splits the garden into four parts?
exercises.hint: Look at the blue lines crossing in the middle.
exercises.explain: Two water channels cross at a pool, making four equal parts.

exercises.hint: He wanted all his peoples treated alike.
exercises.explain: A special tax paid by non-Muslims, so his Hindu subjects were treated more equally.

exercises.prompt: Why did Akbar hold debates between people of many faiths?
choices: to understand their faiths and keep the peace
exercises.explain: He wanted to understand their beliefs, and respect helped keep peace in a land of many faiths.

exercises.prompt: The Taj Mahal is built so that its left and right halves mirror each other.
exercises.hint: Look at the picture of its front.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: built by the Mughals, or by the Ottomans?
exercises.hint: The Mughals ruled India; the Ottomans ruled from Istanbul.
exercises.explain: Mughals: the Taj Mahal, Fatehpur Sikri, the Red Fort. Ottomans: the Süleymaniye Mosque, Topkapi Palace, Iznik tiles.

exercises.prompt: Put these Mughal emperors in order.
exercises.hint: Look at the years each began to rule.
exercises.explain: Babur 1526, Akbar 1556, Jahangir 1605, Shah Jahan 1628, Aurangzeb 1658.

exercises.prompt: About 20,000 workers built the Taj Mahal. If they worked in teams of 250, how many teams were there?
exercises.hint: Divide the workers by the size of a team.
